subQuestions.questionText:
The hormone responsible for the regulation of salt content in the human body is …
A testosterone.
B aldosterone.
C prolactin.
D glucagon.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Aldosterone (secreted by the adrenal cortex) regulates the salt (sodium) content of the blood. Testosterone controls male secondary characteristics, prolactin stimulates milk production, and glucagon raises blood glucose.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following is a stage in human embryonic development?
A Choroid
B Amnion
C Morula
D Chorion
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
The morula is an early stage of embryonic development, a solid ball of cells formed by mitotic division of the zygote. The choroid is a layer of the eye, while the amnion and chorion are embryonic membranes, not developmental stages.

subQuestions.questionText:
When the carbon dioxide level in the blood increases above normal, the …
A rate and depth of breathing decrease.
B receptor cells in the diaphragm are stimulated.
C heart beats slower.
D receptor cells in the carotid artery in the neck are stimulated.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
A rise in blood carbon dioxide is detected by chemoreceptor cells in the carotid artery in the neck (and the aorta), which trigger an increase in the rate and depth of breathing to expel the excess carbon dioxide.

options.A: rate and depth of breathing decrease.
options.B: receptor cells in the diaphragm are stimulated.
options.D: receptor cells in the carotid artery in the neck are stimulated.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following changes occurs under the influence of adrenalin?
A An increased blood supply to the skeletal muscles
B Decreased blood pressure
C Decreased muscle tone of skeletal muscles
D An increased blood supply to the digestive system
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Adrenalin prepares the body for 'fight or flight': it increases blood supply to the skeletal muscles, raises blood pressure and heart rate, and diverts blood away from the digestive system.

options.A: An increased blood supply to the skeletal muscles
options.C: Decreased muscle tone of skeletal muscles
options.D: An increased blood supply to the digestive system

subQuestions.questionText:
A girl is barefoot and steps onto a thorn, causing a reflex action. Which ONE of the following represents the CORRECT pathway of the reflex arc?
A Pain receptor → motor neuron → sensory neuron → leg muscle
B Foot muscle → sensory neuron → motor neuron → pain receptor
C Foot muscle → motor neuron → sensory neuron → pain receptor
D Pain receptor → sensory neuron → motor neuron → leg muscle
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
In a reflex arc the stimulus is detected by a pain receptor, the impulse travels along a sensory neuron to the spinal cord, then along a motor neuron to the effector (the leg muscle), which responds.

options.A: Pain receptor → motor neuron → sensory neuron → leg muscle
options.B: Foot muscle → sensory neuron → motor neuron → pain receptor
options.C: Foot muscle → motor neuron → sensory neuron → pain receptor
options.D: Pain receptor → sensory neuron → motor neuron → leg muscle

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram represents a part of the human eye. A spectator in a soccer stadium is seated 200 metres away from the field. Which ONE of the following describes the condition of structures X, Y and Z when he looks at the ball placed in the middle of the field?
A Muscle in X: Relaxed; Structure Y: Slack; Part Z: More convex
B Muscle in X: Contracted; Structure Y: Slack; Part Z: Less convex
C Muscle in X: Relaxed; Structure Y: Taut; Part Z: Less convex
D Muscle in X: Contracted; Structure Y: Taut; Part Z: More convex
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
To focus on a distant object the eye needs minimal accommodation: the ciliary muscle in X is relaxed, the suspensory ligaments (structure Y) are taut, and the lens (part Z) becomes thinner / less convex.

options.A: Muscle in X: Relaxed; Structure Y: Slack; Part Z: More convex
options.B: Muscle in X: Contracted; Structure Y: Slack; Part Z: Less convex
options.C: Muscle in X: Relaxed; Structure Y: Taut; Part Z: Less convex
options.D: Muscle in X: Contracted; Structure Y: Taut; Part Z: More convex

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following is involved in thermoregulation?
A Corpus callosum
B Hypothalamus
C Cerebellum
D Spinal cord
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
The hypothalamus contains the body's thermoregulatory centre, which monitors blood temperature and initiates responses that keep body temperature constant.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following is a list of factors regarding a developing foetus:
(i) Temperature regulation
(ii) Protection
(iii) Free movement
(iv) Nutrition
For which combination of factors is the amniotic fluid responsible?
A (i), (ii) and (iii) only
B (i) and (iv) only
C (ii) and (iii) only
D (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
The amniotic fluid regulates temperature, protects the foetus by cushioning it against mechanical shock, and allows free movement. Nutrition is provided by the placenta, not the amniotic fluid.

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram shows a part of the human ear. Which ONE of the following occurs when there are excess waves in the inner ear?
A Pressure is released at A
B Pressure is released at C
C Pressure is absorbed at B
D Pressure is absorbed at A and C
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Excess pressure waves in the fluid of the inner ear are absorbed at B (the round window), which prevents echoes and damage to the receptors.

options.D: Pressure is absorbed at A and C

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagrams represent the transmission of impulses from a structure in the inner ear to the brain (letters E, F, G, H and J). The nerve impulses for balance are transmitted as follows:
A J → F → H
B E → F → H
C E → F → G
D J → F → G
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
The impulses concerned with balance follow the pathway E → F → H from the balance receptor in the inner ear along the nerve to the brain.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none of the items in COLUMN II.
Description: Acts as a micro-filter for the developing foetus.
A: Placenta
B: Cervix
subQuestions.memoText:
A only (2 marks)
The placenta acts as a selective micro-filter that allows exchange of substances between the mother and the foetus while keeping their blood separate.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none of the items in COLUMN II.
Description: The part of the brain that controls heart rate.
A: Corpus callosum
B: Medulla oblongata
subQuestions.memoText:
B only (2 marks)
The medulla oblongata controls involuntary functions such as heart rate. The corpus callosum connects the two cerebral hemispheres.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none of the items in COLUMN II.
Description: The area on the retina where there are no rods or cones.
A: Blind spot
B: Cornea
subQuestions.memoText:
A only (2 marks)
The blind spot is the area of the retina where the optic nerve leaves the eye and has no rods or cones. The cornea is the transparent front layer of the eye, not part of the retina.

Any 3 of the following (3 marks):

- to provide nutrients / oxygen OR remove waste products

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the passage below.
CATARACTS – THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF BLINDNESS
Cataracts are primarily formed when protein structures in the lens of the eye start to disintegrate and clump together. Cataracts is the most common cause of blindness and the main cause of vision loss in people over 40 years of age. Two types of cataracts that occur are nuclear cataracts and subcapsular cataracts. In nuclear cataracts, the cataracts form in the central region of the lens and gradually spread outwards. In subcapsular cataracts, the cataracts develop at the back of the lens and it is most common in people with diabetes.
According to the passage, which type of cataract is associated with a disorder of the pancreas?
subQuestions.memoText: Sub-capsular cataracts (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Using information in the passage about cataracts (protein structures in the lens disintegrate and clump together), explain why cataracts cause vision loss.
subQuestions.memoText:
(5 marks)
- Protein structures in the lens start to disintegrate and clump together ✓
- The lens becomes opaque ✓ / milky and
- less / no light passes through ✓ the lens
- onto the retina ✓
- therefore less / no stimuli will be converted to impulses ✓

subQuestions.questionText:
The passage below describes the breeding habits of vultures.
Vultures are birds of prey that feed on the flesh of dead animals. A female vulture lays only one to two fertilised eggs, which are then protected by both parents during incubation. Incubation is the period from the time an egg is laid up to the time it hatches. Vultures have a short incubation period of 32 to 45 days. This short incubation period is typical of birds displaying altricial development. After hatching, the parents feed the young chicks as often as 20 times a day.
Give ONE reason from the passage why vultures:
(a) Are considered as oviparous (1)
(b) Have a high survival rate even though few eggs are laid (1)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) They lay eggs (1 mark)
(b) Any ONE (1 mark). Mark first ONE only:
- The eggs are protected / incubated by the parents
- The young chicks are fed by the parents / display parental care

subQuestions.questionText: Fertilisation in vultures takes place internally. State TWO advantages of internal fertilisation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (2 marks). Mark first TWO only:
- It increases the chances of fertilisation / gametes are in close contact
- Gametes are protected from predation / desiccation / environmental factors
- Water is not needed
- Fewer gametes are needed

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO characteristics of chicks that display altricial development.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (2 marks). Mark first TWO only:
- Eyes are closed when they hatch
- Bodies do not have (down) feathers
- Unable to move directly after hatching
- Dependent on parents for food / protection

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why birds with altricial development would have short incubation periods.
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks)
- The chicks are not fully developed when hatched since
- the eggs have less yolk / there is a high degree of parental care

subQuestions.questionText:
An investigation was conducted to determine the effect of insulin on blood glucose levels.
Procedure:
• Two groups of ten people each were selected.
• One of the groups consisted of healthy individuals and the second group, which served as a control, consisted of people with diabetes.
• Each group was given 75 g of glucose to ingest.
• Their blood was tested again after 60 and 90 minutes to determine the levels of glucose and insulin.
NOTE: The normal level of glucose in the blood is between 3,9 mmol/ℓ and 5,6 mmol/ℓ. The normal level of insulin in the blood, 60 minutes after glucose ingestion, is between 18 mU/ℓ and 276 mU/ℓ.
Results (time after glucose ingestion in minutes: 0 / 60 / 90):
Group X – glucose (mmol/ℓ): 6,8 / 8,9 / 8,7 ; insulin (mU/ℓ): 4 / 2 / 2
Group Y – glucose (mmol/ℓ): 4,5 / 6,2 / 4,5 ; insulin (mU/ℓ): 8 / 142 / 108
State the purpose of the control group in this investigation.
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks)
To ensure that the change in blood glucose levels was due to insulin only

subQuestions.questionText: Describe TWO ways in which insulin decreases blood glucose levels.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (2 x 2 = 4 marks). Mark first TWO only:
- It stimulates the absorption of glucose from the blood into the cells
- It stimulates the liver / muscles to convert glucose to glycogen
- It causes increased cellular respiration which utilises glucose

subQuestions.questionText: Using the results table for Group X and Group Y (glucose and insulin levels at 0, 60 and 90 minutes; normal glucose 3,9–5,6 mmol/ℓ), which group (X or Y) consists of healthy individuals?
subQuestions.memoText: Group Y ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Use data in the table (Group X glucose 6,8 / 8,9 / 8,7 mmol/ℓ and insulin 4 / 2 / 2 mU/ℓ; Group Y glucose 4,5 / 6,2 / 4,5 mmol/ℓ and insulin 8 / 142 / 108 mU/ℓ at 0, 60 and 90 minutes) to explain your answer to QUESTION 3.3.3.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3 of the following (3 marks):
- At 0 min, the blood glucose level for group Y was within the normal range / the blood glucose level for group X was high
- At 90 minutes the blood glucose level for group Y returned to normal / the blood glucose levels for group X remained high
- After the ingestion of glucose, the insulin level for group Y increased / the insulin level for group X decreased

subQuestions.questionText:
An investigation was conducted to determine the effect of auxins on plant tropism.
Procedure:
• Twelve plants of the same species were divided into three groups (group A, B and C), of four plants each.
• All the plants were kept in darkness for 72 hours during the investigation.
• The growing tips of group A received no treatment.
• The growing tips of group B were cut off and replaced by a piece of agar that contained auxins (agar is a jelly-like substance through which other substances can diffuse).
• The growing tips of group C were cut off and replaced by a piece of agar without auxins.
For this investigation give:
(a) The independent variable (1)
(b) TWO variables that were controlled (2)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) (Presence of) auxins (1 mark)
(b) Any TWO (2 marks). Mark first TWO only:
- Species
- Light
- Duration in the dark

subQuestions.questionText:
In the auxin and plant tropism investigation, give the expected results of the plants in:
(a) Group A (received no treatment on the growing tips) (1)
(b) Group C (growing tips replaced with agar without auxins) (1)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) The plant / stem grows (straight) upwards (1 mark)
(b) Any ONE (1 mark):
- No upward growth will occur
- Lateral branches will develop

subQuestions.questionText: How was the reliability of this investigation ensured?
subQuestions.memoText: Four plants in each group (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: After 72 hours, the stems of the plants in group B (growing tips replaced with agar containing auxins) bent towards the right-hand side. Explain these results.
subQuestions.memoText:
(4 marks)
- The auxins diffuse into the left side of the stem
- The higher concentration of auxins on the left side
- results in more cell elongation / growth of cells on the left side
- There is less growth on the right-hand side and the stem will bend to the right-hand side
